newsitem.title: FRANCE: LUXEMBOURG SETS OUT ITS EU PRESIDENCY PRIORITIES.
newsitem.headline: LUXEMBOURG SETS OUT ITS EU PRESIDENCY PRIORITIES.

text.p: The European Union must make a final decision in December on its strategy for eastward expansion, including internal reforms, Luxembourg Foreign Minister Jacques Poos told the European Parliament on Wednesday.

Poos, whose country took over the six-month presidency of the 15-member EU bloc on July 1, said EU leaders needed to make "a clear decision" on how to extend the Union at their December 12-13 summit in Luxembourg.
He was speaking on the day the European Commission recommended that negotiations for EU membership should start in early 1998 with five out of 10 east European applicant states and Cyprus.
Luxembourg has the delicate task of working out the method by which the enlargement talks will proceed, and which applicants will be involved in the first round.

Poos said Luxembourg would also concentrate during its six-month stint at the EU helm on making practical steps towards introducing a single European currency and launching a united EU battle against unemployment, drugs and crime.

With increasing demands for Europe to do more to fight unemployment, Luxembourg has been given the task of organising a summit on jobs in the autumn, with November 22 now pencilled in as a possible date.
Attention would also be paid to other facets of social policy, including better procedures for consulting and informing workers on major restructuring decisions, Poos said.

The last few months have seen heated discussions on worker participation in company decisions, following the much criticised decision by French car-maker Renault to shut its profitable assembly plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium, with the loss of 3,100 jobs.

On the economic side, Luxembourg would give priority to launching the Commission's four-point action plan for completing the EU single market and try to make progress on controversial proposals for EU-wide direct and indirect tax regimes, Poos said.

Looking beyond the Union's frontiers, Luxembourg would concentrate the EU's foreign policy efforts on difusing conflict in Cyprus -- a candidate for EU membership -- the Middle East, the former Yugoslavia and Central Africa, he said.

Poos warned further EU aid to Bosnia-Herzogovina would depend on that country's willingness to create effective political and legal institutions, hold free and fair elections in September, allow refugees to return home safely and hand war criminals to the international tribunal in the Hague.
